editorial.marketOverview: Reuters reports Nasdaq opened 3.31% lower against a 1.95% S&P decline. This confirms the weak premarket setup in cash trading, with technology underperformance of 1.36 percentage points at the open.
editorial.whatChanged: The prior assessment lacked cash-session confirmation. The opening decline now confirms risk aversion, while Guardian reporting describes concrete tariff proposals subject to consultation rather than merely anticipated measures. Open Watch remains unchanged.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The opening response is consistent with AI valuation and trade risk dominating any support from lower yields. Headline PCE matched expectations according to Investopedia; strong GDP and persistent core inflation leave policy relief uncertain. No fresh synchronized yield curve or direct SOX/VXN panel is available.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday now has a confirmed weak opening and downside bias, with intraday reversal risk. Friday's shortened session may amplify volatility. Monday depends on whether chip leadership recovers and weekend oil policy changes inflation risk.
editorial.bullCase: A reversal of opening losses with broad chip participation could indicate capitulation rather than continuing liquidation. In-line headline inflation and resilient output provide potential support, not a confirmed recovery.
editorial.bearCase: Failure to recover opening losses would reinforce the selloff, especially if chip underperformance persists and tariff proposals raise cost uncertainty. Lower yields may reflect defensive demand rather than policy relief.
editorial.watchNext: Track QQQ and SOX relative strength, cash breadth, VXN/VIX, paired yields and updated Fed pricing. Watch Beige Book at 14:00 ET, Friday early close and weekend OPEC+ news; verify any additional earnings catalysts.
